req.title: Basic-auth accepts correct credentials
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> with HTTP 200 and an authenticated=true JSON body when the supplied Basic credentials match.

doc.reasoning: The requirement covers GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> returning HTTP 200 with {authenticated: true, user: <user>} when correct Basic credentials are supplied. I design: (1) a positive EP test with matching credentials, asserting exact status and exact JSON body fields; (2) a negative NEG test with wrong password, asserting exact 401 status and WWW-Authenticate header; (3) a boundary BVA test with no Authorization header at all, asserting 401; (4) a DT test covering wrong username but correct password; (5) a positive test with special characters in credentials to cover encoding paths. Each test asserts exact values to kill comparison-flip, boolean-negation, and constant-bump mutations.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_and_authenticated_true
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/testuser/testpass with Authorization: Basic base64(testuser:testpass)
expected: Response JSON body has authenticated == True
trace: R-HTTPBIN-018: correct credentials -> HTTP 200 + {authenticated: true, user: <user>}
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_and_authenticated_true():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'testuser:testpass').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/testuser/testpass',
        headers={'Authorization': 'Basic ' + creds}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['authenticated'] == True
    assert body['user'] == 'testuser'

test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_and_authenticated_true()

tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_response_body_exact_fields():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'alice:secret').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/alice/secret',
        headers={'Authorization': 'Basic ' + creds}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert set(body.keys()) == {'authenticated', 'user'}
    assert body['authenticated'] is True
    assert body['user'] == 'alice'

tests.name: test_basic_auth_user_reflected_in_body_not_hardcoded
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
A different username is used to verify user field is dynamic
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/bob/mypassword with Authorization: Basic base64(bob:mypassword)
expected: JSON body user field is exactly 'bob' (not 'alice' or any hardcoded value)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-018: user field must reflect path param, not be hardcoded; catches constant-substitution mutation
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_user_reflected_in_body_not_hardcoded():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'bob:mypassword').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/bob/mypassword',
        headers={'Authorization': 'Basic ' + creds}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['user'] == 'bob'
    assert body['user'] != 'alice'
    assert body['authenticated'] is True

test_basic_auth_user_reflected_in_body_not_hardcoded()

from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_authenticated_false_not_returned_on_success():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'carol:pass123').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/carol/pass123',
        headers={'Authorization': 'Basic ' + creds}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['authenticated'] is True
    assert body['authenticated'] is not False
